overview.problem: traktor-nml-tool's NiceGUI wizard app has no route through which an operator can build an NML playlist from a base collection and a supplied Artist/Title tracklist matched via the existing matching cascade; that operation exists only as the build-playlist CLI subcommand.
overview.approach: Add a third route, /build-playlist, to the wizard shell, following navigation.py's existing tab table (DL-129..DL-147) rather than a new mechanism. A nicegui-free traktor_nml/gui/buildplaylist_view.py module holds the screen's form validation and report formatting, matching the nicegui-boundary convention review_model.py/wizard_state.py already set for the reconnect wizard. The page itself drives buildplaylist.assemble_output, rewrite.py's path-collision and atomic-write helpers, and split.py's isolation pass directly, in the same order build_playlist_cmd.py already calls them, so the CLI's own behavior and output bytes are untouched and no matching or assembly logic is reimplemented in gui/. The first pass ships a read-only unresolved-lines report rather than an interactive per-line review workflow, which Specs.dc.html's own scope-fence note defers to a later entry point; a design/build-playlist/Specs.dc.html artboard is drafted first as that note's own design of record for the screen.

decisions.decision: The build-playlist screen is a standalone route at /build-playlist with its own single-page form, not a step folded into the reconnect wizard's stepper or the reconstruct page's step rail.
decisions.reasoning: design/reconnect-wizard/Specs.dc.html's scope-fence note states build-playlist 'has its own review model, and is not in Phase 1' and 'is its own entry point, not a branch of this one' -> the design of record already rules out grafting it onto either existing flow -> the new screen answers a third route, following navigation.py's existing table mechanism rather than a new one.

decisions.decision: A nicegui-free traktor_nml/gui/buildplaylist_view.py module holds the build-playlist screen's form validation, invocation-argument shaping, and unresolved-row/report formatting; app.py imports it rather than holding that logic itself.
decisions.reasoning: traktor_nml/gui/CLAUDE.md's nicegui-boundary convention (DL-069) keeps everything reducible to data/arithmetic in a module the system pytest interpreter (no nicegui installed) can import directly -> review_model.py and wizard_state.py are the established shape for this on the reconnect wizard -> the build-playlist screen's own form/report logic takes the same shape rather than living untested inside app.py's wiring.

decisions.decision: The GUI drives traktor_nml/buildplaylist.py's assemble_output, traktor_nml/rewrite.py's path_collides/read_and_parse_source/write_bytes_atomically, and traktor_nml/split.py's build_output directly, mirroring build_playlist_cmd.py's own sequencing (collision refusal, decode, assemble, optional isolation pass, atomic write) without calling the CLI handler or building an argparse Namespace.
decisions.reasoning: The MUST constraint forbids reimplementing matching, resolution or NML node synthesis in gui/, and a MUST NOT constraint forbids changing build_playlist_cmd.py's CLI behavior or output bytes -> app.py already drives reconnect_run/splice cores directly rather than shelling out to their CLI handlers, the established precedent for a second thin surface over one core -> the build-playlist screen takes the same shape, reusing the core modules' functions in the same order build_playlist_cmd.py calls them.

decisions.decision: navigation.SECTIONS gains a third row, ("/build-playlist", "Build playlist"), appended after the existing reconstruct and reconnect rows, with no change to header_tabs' selection rule.
decisions.reasoning: docs/plans/2026-09-03-header-tabs (DL-129..DL-147) already settled the tab mechanism after enumerating pitfalls with route-membership checks and label-based selection (a route prefix wrongly matching more than one tab, a renamed label silently breaking selection) -> the MUST constraint requires following that settled mechanism exactly, i.e. equality comparison against exactly one route, never membership -> a third row is therefore the minimal, precedent-following change (one tuple appended to SECTIONS) rather than a new selection mechanism or a third comparison rule.

decisions.decision: The first shipped build-playlist screen shows unresolved tracklist lines as a read-only report (line, raw text, kind) beside an Allow unmatched toggle mirroring --allow-unmatched, rather than an interactive per-line accept/reject/pick review workflow.
decisions.reasoning: The OUT-OF-SCOPE note flags a full review/conflict-resolution UI as a possible follow-on milestone, not assumed in scope -> buildplaylist.assemble_output already returns unresolved_rows whether or not the run aborts (DL-027, DL-034) -> a read-only report over that same data satisfies a first pass without inventing a decision-state model this plan does not schedule.

decisions.decision: A design/build-playlist/Specs.dc.html artboard is drafted before the GUI requirements for the screen's inputs and report layout are finalized, and is the milestone this plan opens with.
decisions.reasoning: Specs.dc.html's own scope-fence note states build-playlist 'has its own review model' and 'is its own entry point' -> DL-071's precedent treats an artboard as the design of record governing what the operator sees and presses, with a Specs-vs-code disagreement recorded rather than silently resolved -> the SHOULD constraint asks this to be an explicit early milestone decision, so the artboard is drafted first rather than requirements being written unmoored from one.

decisions.decision: The base collection and the tracklist file are both chosen through gui/file_picker.py's existing pick_file_or_folder, matching the CLI's base/tracklist positional file arguments, rather than a paste-in-text tracklist entry.
decisions.reasoning: The reconnect wizard's own Set up step already gathers its file inputs through pick_file_or_folder rather than an upload or paste control -> a second, different input pattern on a third route would read as an unexplained inconsistency an operator carries between screens -> the existing picker is reused for both files.

decisions.decision: The GUI form omits --dry-run and the --unresolved-report CSV export; a dry run is achieved by simply not clicking Write, and the on-screen read-only unresolved-lines report (DL-264) replaces the CSV export for a first pass rather than also offering a file download.
decisions.reasoning: DL-264 already commits to a read-only on-screen report over BuildPlaylistResult.unresolved_rows, the same data the CLI writes to CSV -> a Write-triggers-the-only-action form has no separate no-op state to name --dry-run, since simply not pressing Write is already a dry run -> a file-download control for the same rows the screen already renders is deferred with the rest of the review UI (OUT-OF-SCOPE), not silently dropped.

decisions.decision: run_summary's sentence tracks build_playlist_cmd.py's own CLI wording for the same underlying condition (unresolved tracks, no entries resolved, target-folder errors, entries written) rather than inventing separate GUI phrasing.
decisions.reasoning: The MUST NOT constraint forbids changing the CLI's own stdout contract, and this plan is GUI-only -> an operator who uses both surfaces should read the same words for the same condition rather than needing to learn two vocabularies for one tool -> run_summary is written as a thin rephrasing of build_playlist_cmd.py's existing print statements, not a new message set.

decisions.decision: A failed base/tracklist read or parse, or a write failure, surfaces through run_summary as a refusal sentence naming the failure, the same way form_errors already surfaces a missing-field refusal, rather than an uncaught exception or a silent no-op; there is no GUI equivalent of the CLI's non-zero exit code.
decisions.reasoning: The CLI answers I/O failures with an exception and a non-zero exit code, but a GUI page has no exit code to return -> DL-261/DL-264 already route business-logic outcomes (unresolved_tracks, no_entries_resolved, target-folder errors) through run_summary's refusal sentence -> an I/O failure is the same kind of run-ending condition and is folded into the same refusal-sentence path rather than left to an unhandled exception.

decisions.decision: The report table does not surface MatchConfidence.LOOSE explicitly; every resolved row in this first pass is, by construction, a LOOSE match, so a confidence column would carry one constant value on every row.
decisions.reasoning: assemble_output resolves tracklist lines via resolve_tracklist at a fixed MatchConfidence.LOOSE because a text-only Artist/Title line has no path/size/time to match on more strictly -> a column whose value never varies gives the operator no decision-relevant signal -> DL-264 already scopes the report to unresolved rows (unparseable/unmatched/ambiguous), and a constant-valued confidence column on matched rows is left out rather than added for its own sake.

decisions.decision: This plan schedules no keyboard-navigation, focus-ring, tab-order or screen-reader/announcement milestone for the build-playlist screen beyond whatever the existing header-tab shell and theme.py already provide.
decisions.reasoning: The reconnect wizard's own keyboard/accessibility work already shipped in the now-frozen plan-tool repo, but that does not obligate every new screen to redo it immediately -> the user has stated this class of work is out of scope for new work until explicitly asked for -> this plan follows that standing preference rather than silently omitting the topic or scheduling it unasked.

decisions.decision: The build-playlist form's output path is not a separate literal path chooser; it is derived by combining the playlist name field with the optional target-folder field (relative to the base collection's own directory when target-folder is empty), the same way rewrite.path_collides and the write step consume it.
decisions.reasoning: build_playlist_cmd.py's own 'output' is a required positional distinct from --name and --target-folder, but M-001's enumerated controls (base chooser, tracklist chooser, name, target folder, two switches, Write, report) name no separate output-path input -> asking the operator to type or browse to a full output path duplicates information already captured by name+target-folder and invites a mismatch between the two -> the GUI derives the output path from name+target-folder before calling path_collides, so the same two fields already in the form fully determine the write destination the CLI checks and writes.

risks.risk: README.md's DL high-water mark can move again before this plan mints DL-260 onward: same-day work lands on this package without a docs/plans/ directory of its own, and an implemented block taking DL-260 upward would collide with this one.

risks.mitigation: tests/test_gui_view_boundary.py::test_only_app_file_picker_and_main_import_the_framework already AST-walks every module under traktor_nml/gui/ and asserts only app.py, file_picker.py and __main__.py import the framework, so it automatically catches a regression in the new buildplaylist_view.py without needing a per-module extension (CI-M-003-002).

invisible_knowledge.system: traktor-nml-tool is a CLI+GUI package for repairing/rebuilding Traktor NML collection and playlist files. The GUI is a NiceGUI app with a header-tab shell: '/' serves the 'reconstruct' page, '/reconnect' serves the reconnect wizard, and this plan adds '/build-playlist' as a third route, all sharing one header (navigation.py + theme.py) built by docs/plans/2026-09-03-header-tabs. Every write command in the package pairs a thin commands/ CLI surface with a core module holding the real logic (splice.py/splice_cmd.py, split.py/split_cmd.py, buildplaylist.py/build_playlist_cmd.py); the GUI is a second thin surface over the same core modules the CLI already drives, never a third place logic can drift. Within gui/, everything reducible to data/arithmetic (status derivation, decision state, filter predicates, token tables, tab selection, and now build-playlist's form validation/report formatting) lives in a nicegui-free module the system pytest interpreter can import directly, while app.py itself holds only wiring and is tested instead through a served-page browser-record gate.
invariants: Thin-surface layering: every write command pairs a commands/ CLI surface with a core module (splice.py/splice_cmd.py, split.py/split_cmd.py, buildplaylist.py/build_playlist_cmd.py); the GUI is a second thin surface over the same core modules, never reimplementing matching, resolution or NML node synthesis in gui/.

Nicegui-boundary rule (DL-069): only traktor_nml/gui/app.py, file_picker.py and __main__.py import nicegui/pywebview; every other gui/ module, including buildplaylist_view.py, stays importable on the system pytest interpreter with no nicegui installed, guarded automatically by tests/test_gui_view_boundary.py's AST walk.

A playlist built from external tracklist text has no source span in the base NML (DL-028), so buildplaylist.assemble_output's fragment always takes the ElementTree-serialization path rather than transplantation - relevant if the GUI ever previews the fragment before writing.
tradeoffs: Read-only unresolved-lines report vs. an interactive per-line review/conflict-resolution workflow: the first shipped screen takes the read-only report (DL-264), trading immediate resolve-in-place convenience for a smaller, precedent-following first pass; a full review UI is flagged as a possible follow-on milestone, not assumed in scope.

DL-028's constraint that an externally-sourced playlist has no source span and always takes the ElementTree-serialization path (rather than the byte-span transplantation path other operations can use) is a fixed property of buildplaylist.assemble_output, not a choice this plan makes, but it bounds what the GUI can ever preview about the fragment before writing.
